# measurement-eras.tsv — the eras a baseline can belong to. Tab-separated, tracked.
# WHY ERAS EXIST. A baseline is a number measured by an instrument, and when the
# instrument changes the number changes with it for reasons that are not the host's
# code. Judging a pinned reading against a baseline minted from free-placement draws
# would book the METHODOLOGY DELTA AS HOST DRIFT — the cross-denominator sin the
# registry exists to prevent, arriving through the registry itself. So a baseline is
# scoped to the era whose instrument produced it, and a criterion may not judge a
# reading from one era against a baseline from another (ruled 2026-08-21, #6).
# AN ERA BOUNDARY IS THE "DATED RE-REGISTRATION CITING A NAMED CHANGE" DOOR, OPENED
# FLEET-WIDE. That door already existed in the registry's law for one host at a time;
# an instrument change opens it for every host at once, which is what makes the
# transition run an era boundary rather than a fleet-wide regression.
# THE LOOPHOLE GUARD, which is the whole reason this is a tracked file and not a
# variable. If an era could be declared by convenience, "new era" would become
# exemption-renewal-by-tweak: any operator wanting a green run would open one and
# every host's BASELINE would come back. So an era exists ONLY with both of:
#   1. a dated DESIGN.md §5 or §7 amendment, cited in the `amendment` column, and
#   2. a both-arms transition archive, cited in `transition_archive`, showing the
#      same fleet measured under the old instrument and the new one.
# Condition 2 cannot exist before the transition run that creates it, so an era is
# LANDED with (1) and PROVISIONAL until (2) is filled in by the reviewed commit that
# lands the era's registrations. Half of it CAN exist beforehand, and for `pinned8` it
# does: the old instrument's arm is 35 preserved archives at archive/free-placement/,
# tracked with the single-draw disclosure rule 16 puts on them (ruled 2026-08-21, #6 —
# the both-arms condition asks for both eras' evidence preserved and mapped, never for
# simultaneous re-measurement, which the mask's refusal-with-no-opt-out makes
# unavailable anyway). What the transition run adds is the pinned half.
# Provisional is a disclosure, not a permission: it
# does not widen what BASELINE covers. What bounds BASELINE is scripts/judged-runs.tsv
# — one row per (host, era) — so each host gets exactly one BASELINE per era whether
# the era is provisional or closed.
# THE ERA ID IS NOT THE CONFIGURATION KEY, and conflating the two is the mistake this
# note exists to stop (added 2026-08-22, ruling on #115). `pinned8` has now been founded
# three times without ever closing — confined mask + ceiling instrument v1, spread mask
# + v1, spread + v2 — so its id alone cannot tell a reader which instrument produced a
# given archive. Minting a fresh id per configuration was considered and refused: it
# would rename the era in nine files to encode something the ARTIFACTS ALREADY CARRY.
# Each configuration self-identifies in its own rows — the confined archives by having
# no `doms=`/`nodedoms=` field, the v1 ceilings by having no `instrument=` field, and
# everything after by printing both. So the division of labour is: the era id scopes
# REGISTRATIONS (§5 rule 17's one-BASELINE-per-host-per-era bound), and the artifact
# fields scope CONFIGURATIONS (§7 rule 7's placement-and-version disclosure). What
# makes the re-foundings free of the loophole the guard below exists for is countable
# rather than argued: scripts/judged-runs.tsv has NO data rows and
# scripts/host-baselines.tsv is header-only, so no host has ever spent a BASELINE in
# this era and re-opening it returns nobody's exemption.
# The CURRENT era is the last data row. A row whose `amendment` is empty or `—` is
# not an era: era resolution fails closed, and a criterion with no era resolves to
# UNMEASURED rather than falling back to some other era's baseline.
# columns, tab-separated:
#   1 era                 the id baselines and judged-run rows are scoped by
#   2 opened              the date the amendment landed
#   3 amendment           the dated §5/§7 rule this era's instrument change was ruled by
#   4 transition_archive  the both-arms archive; `—` while provisional
#   5 grounds             what changed about the instrument, in one clause

column3: DESIGN.md §5 rule 5 (2026-08-21, placement is pinned fleet-wide and never selectively; amended 2026-08-22 to one core per cache domain, FINAL the same day) + §5 rule 18 (2026-08-22, the ceiling instrument measures the wrong noun; v1 readings are era-scoped and not re-adjudicated) + §5 rule 17 (the era clause)
column4: CLOSED 2026-08-28. Free arm: archive/free-placement/, 35 archives, INDEX.tsv. Pinned arm: archive/pinned8/, 24 confined (INDEX.tsv) + 21 spread (INDEX-spread.tsv, 9 ladder at instrument=v2 and 12 clock-window). All three JUDGED CPU models are present in both arms — AMD EPYC 9R14 11 free/4 confined/3 spread, AMD EPYC 9R45 10/5/3, Intel 8124M 6/15/3 — counted by the measured predicate, not by name: spread self-identifies by carrying doms=/nodedoms= and confined by lacking it, so the two indexes partition the directory and each is the other's complement. Intel 6975P-C is 8 free / 0 pinned, the stated exclusion named below and not a gap in this condition
column5: every judged invocation and its ceiling arm run under one CPU affinity mask of eight distinct physical cores within a single NUMA node, ONE PER CACHE DOMAIN, enumerated deterministically. Rows carry `-8` where the free arm carried `-192` or `-72`, and each archive records the domain of every masked core plus the count its node offered, so the shape is checkable off the artifact. NO LONGER PROVISIONAL (2026-08-28): the spread-form campaign that produces the pinned half has run, and its 21 archives are preserved and indexed beside the confined ones, so transition_archive is filled and this era is closed. What forced the preservation was not tidiness: the published README rows cited their evidence as `build/` paths, and build/ is gitignored, so the 24 published numbers rested on logs that existed on one operator's machine and nowhere in the repo — #114's defect at the publication layer. The FREE half exists — archive/free-placement/, 35 archives, single draws. The 24 archives at archive/pinned8/ are the CONFINED arm, taken 2026-08-21..22 under the first form of the mask, which on EPYC 9R45 landed all eight cores in one CCD and measured 5.96x (dot) / 4.65x (axpy) less stream bandwidth than the spread form — preserved as the provisional arm and superseded by the 2026-08-22 amendment, and self-identifying as pre-amendment by carrying no doms=/nodedoms= field. Per the 2026-08-22 ruling on #6 the both-arms condition is scoped to JUDGED hosts, so keel-gnr (characterization, 8 free archives, 0 pinned) is a stated exclusion here rather than an unmet condition. THE MASK IS NOW FINAL on the spread form (2026-08-22) and the CEILING INSTRUMENT IS v2: every ceiling reading taken before that repair forked eight goroutines and joined them inside each b.N iteration, so 22% of its timed region was convening rather than computing, and the bias was host- and mask-dependent AND VARIED PER RUN — which is why those readings are marked instrument-v1 and left where they stand rather than corrected by any formula (§5 rule 18). Nothing needed recovering: no bar was typed from them, no registry row landed from them, no verdict rests on them. What this costs is a third founding run, and the reason it costs only that is pre-commitment — had CEIL_FRACTION been typed at the 74.3% the v1 ceilings supported, the repair would now be forcing a published bar retraction instead of filling in a version label
